title: Restriction of the finite-type kernel condition to an open subscheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose that for every open $U\subseteq X$, every $n\in\mathbb N$ and every map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to F|_U$, the kernel is of finite type in the sense of [pqf-def-coherent]. For an open $W\subseteq X$, restriction is as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Then for every open $V\subseteq W$, every $n\in\mathbb N$, and every map $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}\to (F|_W)|_V$, its kernel is of finite type. No finite-type hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Definitions 01BV (definition-coherent), 01B5 (definition-finite-type), and Section 01AF (section-kernels); read at the official Stacks tag pages

proof.text: Set U = W.ι image V. Scheme.Hom.isoImage gives the canonical isomorphism s : V.toScheme ≅ U.toScheme. Compose Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U, restriction along s.hom (an equivalence with inverse restriction along s.inv), and the inverse of Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V. The restriction composition and congruence isomorphisms, together with isoImage_hom_ι, give an isomorphism T(F.over U) ≅ (F restricted to W).over V. The unit comparison isomorphisms show T preserves the structure module.

Mathlib SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso identifies T of the rank-n free module with the rank-n free module over V, since equivalences preserve coproducts. Use fullness of T to pull back the conjugate of the given morphism to a morphism g over U. The assumed kernel condition gives finite type of kernel g. PreservesKernel.iso and kernel.mapIso identify T(kernel g) with kernel f.

Prove finite-type transport directly using local generators: transport every finite generating family through the pushforward on the corresponding slice sites; these functors preserve coproducts and epimorphisms. Cocontinuity lifts the covering of the terminal object. Shrink the index type of the resulting local generators to the module universe. Apply this to the two open-site module equivalences and to restriction along s.hom, then transport through the kernel isomorphism. The construction uses no nonempty-open or positive-rank assumption, so also applies to the empty open and n = 0.

proof_origin.place: Definitions 01BV (definition-coherent), 01B5 (definition-finite-type), and Section 01AF (section-kernels), checked at the official Stacks tag pages. E4 formalization: use the canonical isomorphism of the nested open with its image rather than the iterated-slice equivalence; finite-generator transport follows the proved private argument in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.QuasicoherentFiniteTypeAffine.
